assertions: Lilly will purchase Master B.'s houses — the bargain will be perfected and he will deal successfully with the seller
The seller will treat favourably with him and will abate something from the first demand of £530, the price coming to a lower, agreeable sum

Money will be procured to pay for the purchase, though not without difficulty and delay — the retrograde lord of the 2nd shows his own money cannot be called in at once and must be waited for or raised with effort
The delay is in timing and negotiation (square translation, retrograde and cadent lord of the 4th), not a breaking-off: completion is slow rather than denied
The houses themselves are sound and worth buying — Saturn lord of the 4th has no material debility beyond retrogradation and cadency, no hidden ruin or fraud in the property defeats the purchase
His hopes in the matter will be fulfilled, the lord of the 7th being also lord of the 11th and the seller's significator the Sun in the 7th being received by exalted Venus
summary: Yes — Lilly should and will buy the houses, at less than the £530 first asked, with the money found though only after difficulty and delay.
method: Lilly horary (whole-sign/classical horary): significators 1st/2nd/4th/7th/11th, reception, application and translation of light
reasoning: Venus in exaltation near the 7th cusp receives the Sun, significator of the seller in the 7th, so the seller is disposed to receive and deal with Lilly. Venus applying by trine to Saturn, lord of the 4th (the houses), perfects the matter easily between buyer-side benefic and property. Lord of 7th being also lord of 11th ties the seller to Lilly's hopes. Moon translating light, albeit by square out of signs of long ascension, still brings significators together — perfection with friction, not prohibition. Against speed only: Mercury lord of the 2nd retrograde (money locked up / not callable for months) and Saturn retrograde and cadent, which delay payment and possession but do not deny them, Saturn otherwise lacking material debility.
